audit-everyday-mismatch.why: everyday board cells compared against their own linked product's per-unit - the only check that asks whether the number we PUBLISHED agrees with the page we LINKED to. Measured 2026-07-31: 2,582 checked, 0 uncomputable, 0 without a board per-unit, 5 findings. Board-derived like guards/4-factor (2,582 on the same board), so the same measured 0.10 band applies. THIS CHECK WAS AN ORPHAN until 2026-07-31 - it ran nowhere, so its own history starts here. Eligible counts only everyday cells we hold a link for, so the number does not swing when the board gains sale cells or linkless ones. || WHY IT FELL TO ~2,594, PROVED 2026-08-31 and recorded so nobody re-derives it. The population shrank; the coverage did not. Commit 61d148b0 (2026-08-22) stopped carry-forward resurrecting products a store had stopped selling - it had been carrying any item absent from a pull, which is right for the ~590 terms a rotation never touches and WRONG for a term the pull DID search and that did not come back. 344 Aldi rows plus 186 pre-contract rows were retired that day. The ledger shows exactly that shape: a step from ~2,900 to ~2,500 on 2026-08-22 and flat since, not a slide. Today: examined 2,594 of 2,614 eligible, 99.2%. The 20 unexamined are NOT rows it stopped looking at - eligible = checked + uncomputable-size + no-board-per-unit, so they are cells this check structurally cannot compare. THE FLOOR IS DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 2,968 rather than accepted down: -AcceptLower is all-or-nothing across every dropped row, and of the six it would lower this is the ONLY one in breach - audit-ff-carry is RATCHET DELIBERATELY OFF by its own note, and pin-derivable, pin-identity and 4-factor are all inside their tolerances. Lowering five rows that are not in breach to settle one is a net loss of protection. Accept it the day the tool can lower ONE check by name.

audit-ff-carry.why: RATCHET DELIBERATELY OFF - this denominator is INVERSE. It counts EMPTY Family Fare search terms re-probed against Freshop, so the number FALLS when the FF pull gets BETTER (fewer empty terms to re-probe). A ratchet here would fire at whoever fixed the thing it watches, which is worse than no watcher. Pinned by its own clean twin in test-auditors. BLIND still covers the case that matters for this check - it examining nothing at all - which is exactly where it sat on 2026-08-01.

audit-food-category.why: priced cells scanned for a wrong-CLASS product (the blueberries-as-Bai-beverage guard). Measured 2026-07-30: 2663 scanned of 3196 priced cells, 372 skipped because their commodity's category maps to no class list and 161 because the cell carries no product name. Board-derived, so the measured 0.10 band applies. A later same-day board rebuild read 2661 of 3194, well inside the band.

build-rescue-worklist.why: everyday walled-store board cells traced to a dated capture file. Measured on the first real run, 2026-07-31: 1,517 everyday cells across the four walled stores (Walmart 436, Sam's Club 347, Aldi 332, Fareway 402) and all 1,517 traced. Board-derived like guards/4-factor and audit-everyday-mismatch, so the same measured 0.10 band applies. Eligible is everyday cells of the four `walled: true` stores only - sale cells and the three headless stores stay out of the denominator, so the number does not swing on an ad cycle. Examined falls to 0 (BLIND, exit 3) if the capture files vanish from out\, which is the fresh-clone / cloud-runner state: every cell would read UNTRACEABLE and the emitted lists would be a full re-pull rather than a rescue. max_age_days 3 because it runs on the ad cycle, not on every publish.

guards/10-store-charges.why: Wide on purpose: the denominator is every priced row across all store feeds, so it steps whenever a walled store lands a big capture (24,018 -> 29,542 in three days). Narrowing it would cry wolf on a normal Walmart or Sams import. Revisit once coverage-ledger-history.jsonl holds a few weeks of per-check movement.

guards/11-bakers-provenance.why: Bakers is a full API pull, so this is normally flat (6,936 -> 6,947). The width covers a partial Kroger API run rather than day-to-day noise. A candidate for narrowing once history exists.

guards/3-pin-derivable.why: SMALL-N, where a percentage is the wrong instrument: the denominator is override pins (19 today, 1 pin = 5%), and pins collapsed 19 -> 1 in July when generate-board-overrides stopped minting one per same-day pull. A tight percentage here fires on ordinary pin churn, not on lost coverage.

guards/3-pin-identity.why: SMALL-N, same denominator as guards/3-pin-derivable. This is the row that sat at 0 of 16 while the ok line said 16, so BLIND is the verdict that matters for it, not REGRESSED.

guards/4-factor.why: board cells compared against their own linked product's per-unit. The single largest coverage number on the publish path and the one most directly tied to the board, so the measured 0.10 band applies.

guards/5-multipack.why: DEAD RATCHET until 2026-08-01: this was 1.0, which put the regression floor at 0 and made REGRESSED structurally unfirable. 0.5 is deliberately wide and the reason is measured, not guessed - this denominator is driven by how VERBOSE the Walmart capture is (guard 5 counts rows whose NAME states a pack count), and guards.ps1 records that it sat at 0 for every newest-Walmart file from 2026-07-05 to 07-14. A terser capture legitimately halves it; anything past half is the silent no-op guard 5 warns about.

guards/6-collapse.why: SMALL-N: 7 stores, so one store dropping out is -14%. 15% is the tightest band that does not fire when a single store has no capture history (sams today).

guards/9-freshness.why: SMALL-N: 7 stores, same arithmetic as guards/6-collapse.

pull-regular-hyvee.why: DENOMINATOR CHANGED 2026-08-22 - the numbers here are NOT comparable to the 1,010 that stood before, and nothing regressed. Until the capture-policy budget landed (2026-08-20, repaired 2026-08-22) this lane re-verified every product it holds a productId for, every day, and 1,010 was the measured high-water mark of that regime (1,006-1,065 on every file since 2026-07-19). The lane now deliberately asks about ceil(1554/90) = 18 products a day, rotated by a cursor against the 90-day carry, so products-refreshed-today fell to roughly 2-18 BY DESIGN. Left as it was - eligible = all ~535 products holding an id, examined = refreshed today - this row reported a ~98% REGRESSION every single morning: a permanent finding nobody could act on, which is the ledger's own founding failure (a confident answer about nothing) running in reverse, because a watcher that cries daily is one people learn to scroll past. THE PAIR IS NOW TODAY'S SLICE: eligible = the products the run was ALLOWED to ask about today and holds an id to ask with, examined = the ones Aisles Online actually answered with a usable offer for. A healthy day is 3 of 3, not 3 of 535. Examined is `answered`, not `refreshed`: a row whose answer was refused (size mismatch, a price below the store's own shelf tag) WAS examined - counting a refusal as unexamined would report a collapse on a day the accuracy checks did their job. THE ABSOLUTE RATCHET IS DELIBERATELY OFF AND min_ratio REPLACES IT. Measured over a full 90-day rotation of the 2026-08-21 file (1,554 rows, 490 carrying a product id, and the ids CLUSTER): an 18-wide slice offers 0-18 askable products, median 3, mean 5.7. No fixed floor can separate a throttled day from an ordinary one across that range - the fixed floor is what produced the permanent finding above - so the rail is the RATIO of what we got to what we were allowed to ask for. min_ratio 0.90 fires the moment the wall-clock cap starts biting or GraphQL stops answering, which is the truncation this puller was put on the ledger to catch, and it stays quiet on a small slice fully covered. ONE unanswered row is never a shortfall, only a note: on a median 3-product slice a single dead product id would read as a 33% collapse and fire about one morning in seventeen (measured no-offer rate ~2% of asked products - 08-21 landed 490 of 490, 08-18 landed 356 fresh plus 171 capped of 539), while every failure this rail is for misses dozens at once. `examined: 3` is the measured median kept as documentation; -Accept leaves it alone (it prints PINNED), because raising it on a dense 18-product day would re-arm the very floor this row exists to avoid. tolerance 1.0 records that the absolute REGRESSED test is off on purpose, the same way audit-ff-carry does; audit-coverage-ledger skips both REGRESSED and DEAD-RATCHET for a row that declares min_ratio. EXPECT AN INERT DAY ABOUT 5 TIMES A QUARTER. 6% of 18-wide windows in the rotation contain no product holding a link at all (5 of 87 simulated slices), so eligible is legitimately 0 and the lane verifies no price that day. INERT is the true verdict there and it should stay visible: it is the no-discovery-path problem - 1,064 of the 1,554 rows carry no link - in the only form anyone can act on. WHY THIS PULLER IS ON THE LEDGER AT ALL: its own numbers were being thrown away. check-ad-cycles piped it to Out-Null and logged an unconditional success line, so a truncated pull, a collapsed pull and a clean one were identical in the log. max_age_days 3 because it runs on the ad cycle, not on every publish. WHAT THIS METRIC CANNOT ANSWER is whether the rotation KEEPS UP - that is a row-age question, and measured 2026-08-21 the answer is yes: oldest Hy-Vee row 38 days, median 11, zero rows past 60, against a 90-day carry.
